pairs.subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
pairs.evidence: src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:173 The voice gateway holds exactly one person-chosen backend (one Speaker plus one Listener composed by the studio), with no candidate list, fallback tree or caller-selectable schema; a search of src/athena/channels and tests/channels found no failover, fallback list, routing strategy or finish_reason, so the plane this subject governs does not exist here.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:173 Exactly one candidate per direction. A failed backend surfaces as VoiceBackendError and is never swept across alternatives.
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:344 compose() builds one speaker and one listener from the saved choice. There is one candidate set with one policy, and no tree.
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:5 A person pins the engine, so there is no selector to protect. This is the technique's 'decision is not the plane's to own' exclusion.
src/athena/channels/voice/gateway.py:10 The wire contract is the project's own, used by a first-party surface. That is one consumer population, not a mimicked foreign shape.
src/athena/channels/voice/backends.py:86 There are only three engines (Kokoro, whisper.cpp, OpenAI), each hand-coded. That falls under the technique's 'two or three upstreams' exclusion.

pairs.subject: multi-provider-gateway-plane
pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts:7 These files are client libraries for one first-party daemon over loopback, and they only render engine probes and choices the daemon makes. A search of apps/desktop/src/lib found no failover, routing strategy, fallback list or finish_reason, so no multi-provider gateway plane lives in this context.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/src/lib/api.ts:5 There is a single upstream (the local daemon) with nothing to fall back to.
apps/desktop/src/lib/api.ts:13 There is one stream from one upstream, the daemon's own SSE. This is the technique's 'one upstream' exclusion.
apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts:53 The person picks the engine (claude_code or codex) and the client does no selection or substitution.
apps/desktop/src/lib/engines.ts:21 Engine identity comes from fixed CLI ids the daemon probes. No shared-protocol endpoints are discovered here.
